lead.title: TSMC explores collaboration with Elon Musk's Terafab project
lead.summary: TSMC is reportedly weighing a collaboration with Terafab, the Tesla/SpaceX/Intel chip venture being built near Giga Texas, to establish advanced end-to-end semiconductor manufacturing in the United States. The Terafab project targets more than 1 terawatt of AI compute capacity per year at an estimated $20-25 billion cost — a partnership would put the world's most advanced foundry behind Musk's most ambitious AI infrastructure bet.

top_stories.title: Cloudflare releases Clef and Clef-Flash, open-weight 'decision models' under Apache 2.0
top_stories.summary: Cloudflare shipped Clef (27B, post-trained from Qwen3.8-27B) and Clef-Flash (9B, from Qwen3.5-9B): multimodal decision models that return calibrated probabilities over a fixed typed schema instead of free-form text, with 64K context, Ollama support and hosted inference on Workers AI. Cloudflare claims its threat-intel team runs end-to-end website classification in ~2.2s with Clef versus ~4.7s with its fastest general-purpose open LLM, and it also announced an RL fine-tuning platform for custom decision categories.

top_stories.title: CMU trains a 4B proposer that edits agent harness code and beats its 35B teacher
top_stories.summary: A CMU paper trains a proposer model with RL to read a task, the current harness and an execution report, then propose code edits to the harness while the solver model stays frozen. The trained 4B proposer beats its 35B teacher on single-step revisions in Reasoning Gym, including unseen task families, and a HotpotQA-trained version generalizes to MuSiQue and 2WikiMultihopQA.

top_stories.title: AutoCompact: agents trained to compact their own context gain +9.2 points on SWE-bench Verified
top_stories.summary: AutoCompact trains agents via SFT on judge-corrected trajectories plus RL with task-success rewards to decide when to compact context, what working state to preserve, and how to resume — delivering +9.2 points on SWE-bench Verified and +5.0 on SWE-PolyBench Verified, with gains persisting even in very large context windows.

top_stories.title: Simon Willison: AI systems need hard, default-on budget caps
top_stories.summary: After repeated stories of agents racking up surprise bills in retry loops, Simon Willison argues that AI agents and LLM systems should ship with strictly enforced budget caps by default across token usage, cloud spend and API calls — with replies citing real cases, including Netlify moving to credit-based pricing.

items.title: GPT-6 Astra robot agents hit 14% higher task success with 65% fewer tokens
items.summary: PyRUA-Lean is an interactive code-execution framework for VLM robot agents that composes primitives into Python cells with conditional checks and selective observation. Across 700 simulated episodes it reports 14% higher task success with 65% fewer tokens than repeated full-observation invocations.

items.title: LoopCD decodes looped transformers better for (almost) free
items.summary: A training-free contrastive decoding method for looped transformers contrasts the final recurrent pass against an earlier pass in logit space. Recurrence provides aligned weak-and-strong prediction pairs for free, improving next-token selection without auxiliary models or extra training.

items.title: Keyword harnesses fail open: a cheap diagnostic ladder for tool-use claims
items.summary: Documents false positives in keyword-matching tool-use benchmarks: a 661.6M and a 1,109M Spanish security LLM score nearly identically on lenient metrics (0.660 vs 0.650), while verbatim-reproduction checks separate them completely. The authors propose a strict, cheap ladder for verifying tool-use claims.

items.title: ROWBench asks whether video models render what the program specifies
items.summary: A 170-episode, 600-proxy-video benchmark evaluates whether programmable world models visually render fine-grained, program-specified world events, logging entity states and timestamps for fidelity checks that existing visual-quality benchmarks miss.

items.title: AutoGUIWorld uses image generators as visual world models for GUI agents
items.summary: A data-generation framework that uses image generators' visual priors as a visual world model for GUI agents, synthesizing diverse interaction trajectories without deploying and configuring real software environments.

items.title: Kawasaki Heavy aims for a fully autonomous humanoid AI robot by 2030
items.summary: Kawasaki Heavy Industries plans to release the Kaleido android, a fully autonomous humanoid powered by AI, as soon as 2030, built on a domestic Japanese physical-AI platform developed with startup Noetra.

items.title: RoboParty unveils RP1, a full-stack open-source humanoid robot, at IROS 2026
items.summary: Debuted in Pittsburgh, the RP1 is billed as the first high-performance, full-stack open-source platform for embodied AI, with Romomo actuators delivering 160 N·m peak joint torque and unsupervised-RL-trained motor skills. Mechanical files, SDKs and simulation environments are slated for release through late 2026.

items.title: China unveils first humanoid robot stack claimed to be 100% domestically made
items.summary: The Intewell industrial OS, AUTBUS TSN-based bus, MaVIEW agent platform and a domestic AI computing chip power what is claimed to be the first embodied-intelligence humanoid running end-to-end on a fully domestic electronic stack — unveiled in Yichang, Hubei, and framed as bypassing Western technology controls.

items.title: IDC counts ~25,000 humanoid shipments in H1 2026, up 432% year over year
items.summary: Global humanoid shipments reached nearly 25,000 units worth over $740M in the first half of 2026, with China taking 77.9% share and Agibot leading at 8,600+ units. The same roundup notes Tesla cutting Optimus onboard memory capacity to reduce cost, prioritizing bandwidth over capacity.

items.title: jpm: a JavaScript package manager written in Rust, every line by Claude Code
items.summary: A new JS package manager implemented in Rust, with the author stating every line was written by Anthropic's Claude Code agent, pitched on Show HN as a faster, single-binary alternative to npm tooling.

items.title: TechCrunch maps the boom in AI agents that live in your text messages
items.summary: A roundup of the fast-growing category of personal AI agents reachable via SMS, iMessage and WhatsApp — including Instinct, Poke, Folk, Caddy, Fambot and Wajo's Fo. Several agents now get their own email addresses, phone numbers and payment cards to act autonomously on users' behalf.

items.title: SuperLocalMemory 4.0 pitched as a 'Governed Memory Operating System' for agents
items.summary: A Show HN release of a governed local memory layer for AI agents, with an accompanying arXiv paper, positioning itself against cloud memory services by keeping agent memory on-device with governance controls.
